item.source_question_text:
Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can assume a "spherical cow" when analyzing the motion of a cow's leg. [incorrect]
B. We can safely assume a cow is a point mass when analyzing its position change in the scale of a mile over a certain time period. [correct]
C. We can never assume the cow is in a vacuum, even when we need to ignore the effect of air resistance. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect]
item.generated_question_text:
Which of the following statements is correct about choosing a simplified model in physics?
A. It is reasonable to treat a hummingbird as a sphere when analyzing the detailed flapping motion of one wing. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because wing-flap details depend on shape and rotation, so a spherical approximation throws away essential geometry.
B. It is reasonable to treat a delivery van as a point mass when estimating how far it travels along a highway over tens of kilometers. [correct] Explanation: This is correct because the van’s size is negligible compared with kilometer-scale displacements, making a point-mass model appropriate.
C. You are not allowed to assume “vacuum conditions” in a calculation even when you explicitly intend to neglect air resistance. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because assuming vacuum is a standard idealization used precisely to justify ignoring drag.
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because one of the statements (the point-mass approximation over large distances) is a valid modeling choice.

B. It decreases by a factor of 4. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because reducing distance increases force rather than decreasing it.
